held_list.headline: Because of AI, 52% of students with elevated depressive symptoms who used a generative-AI coaching app for six weeks improved meaningfully, against 32% given care as usual.
Because of AI, the Hurricane Center called a Category 5 landfall in Jamaica about three days out, while Melissa was still a Category 1.
Because of AI, Oman screened 43,000 diabetics for retinopathy, flagged 12,000 for treatment, and cut specialist waiting lists by 87%.

Because of AI, specialist consultations at two hospitals in western China took 3.14 minutes instead of 4.41 when patients first gave their history to a chatbot, and patients rated communication easier.
held_list.detail: evidence: drafter A, verifier could not grade.

leads_added: ALERT-PA, cluster-randomized EHR alert for primary aldosteronism screening, 12,501 patients, Brigham and Women's. [NCT05925569](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05925569) (results first posted 2026-11-03). Read in full via the registry record: real patients, randomized by clinician, 2024-03-13 start, primary completion 2024-12-09. Not drafted: the intervention is a rule-based Epic Best Practice Advisory, not AI, so it fails the "AI did something" test. Missing: any indication that the alert uses a model.
Protocol to watch: [AEARCTR-0020106](https://www.socialscienceregistry.org/trials/20106) (physician incentives, managed care vs fee-for-service; in development, 2028 to 2030; not an AI benefit lead).

Skipped: systematic reviews (smoking cessation, LVO stroke), retrospective model validations (cardiac MRI segmentation, osteonecrosis, ILD on notes, ECG foundation models), benchmarks, a qualitative interview study, medical-education items, an AI-moderated interviews methods preprint.
`eagle-cadde-colonoscopy-rct`: the verification record `2026-10-26.json` is still malformed (verifier.tokens has unrecognized keys `cached` and `reasoning`). The gate has to run again.
